summary.title: Elucidating the SNR-t Bias of Diffusion Probabilistic Models

details: Identifies the "SNR-t bias": during training a sample's signal-to-noise ratio is a deterministic function of its timestep, but at inference accumulated network/discretization errors break this coupling, so denoised samples carry an SNR that mismatches their assigned timestep, degrading generation.
Distinguished from previously studied exposure bias (an inter-sample discrepancy); SNR-t bias is argued to be its more fundamental cause.

DCW (Differential Correction in the Wavelet domain): a training-free, NFE-free plug-in that, at each denoising step, adds a scaled difference between the current predicted sample x̂_{t-1} and the model's clean-data reconstruction x_θ^0(x̂_t,t), pushing the sample back toward the ideal noisy state for its timestep.

The correction is applied per wavelet subband (one low-frequency, three high-frequency) with timestep-dependent weights (low-frequency weight emphasized early, high-frequency later, scaled by reverse-process variance σ_t), matching the coarse-to-fine denoising order.

Accompanying theory: under the assumption x_θ^0 = γ_t x_0 + φ_t ε (with γ_t ≤ 1), the reverse sample satisfies x̂_{t-1} = γ̂_{t-1} x_{t-1} + ψ_{t-1} ε, proving its SNR is always below the forward SNR at the same t.
ADM on CIFAR-10, 2,000 samples: feed forward-perturbed x_t into a network fixed at timestep s and measure ||ε_θ(x_t,s)||_2 (sliding-window mismatch test).
Compare E||ε_θ(x_t,t)||_2^2 (forward samples) vs E||ε_θ(x̂_t,t)||_2^2 (reverse-sampled), plus robustness sweeps over seeds (16/42/99) and batch sizes (10/100/1000/2000).
Data-space check of E||x_θ^0||^2 versus ||x_0||^2 to validate γ_t < 1.
Stochastic: IDDPM, ADM, A-DPM, EA-DPM (NPR-DM); deterministic: DDIM, EDM, PFGM++; transformer/T2I: DiT, FLUX, Qwen-Image.
Sampling budgets of 10-50 steps (13/21/35 NFE for EDM and PFGM++), both linear and cosine noise schedules.
CIFAR-10 32x32, CelebA 64x64, ImageNet 128x128 and 256x256, LSUN Bedroom 256x256; FID (primary) and Recall over 50K samples against the full training set.
Qualitative text-to-image comparisons with FLUX and Qwen-Image at 10 and 20 steps.
Compared against DPM-AE and DPM-AT (ICLR 2025) under identical DDIM/ADM settings.
DCW additionally stacked on top of exposure-bias correctors ADM-IP, ADM-ES, and DPM-FR (prior SOTA).
Pixel-space-only correction (DC) vs low-frequency-only (DL) vs high-frequency-only (DH) vs full DCW.
Hyperparameter sweeps for λ_l and λ_h with a two-stage coarse (0.01) then fine (0.001) search; alternative weighting schedules (variance-based, piecewise, constant).
Wall-clock overhead measured on a single A6000, 100 repeated runs per setting.

key_findings.finding: Diffusion networks mispredict systematically when a sample's SNR does not match the conditioning timestep, and reverse-process samples consistently have lower SNR than forward samples at the same timestep.
key_findings.evidence: With a network fixed at timestep s, inputs x_t with t > s (lower SNR) yield overestimated noise norms and t < s yields underestimated norms; separately E||ε_θ(x̂_t,t)||_2 exceeds E||ε_θ(x_t,t)||_2 at every timestep, robust across three seeds and batch sizes 10-2000.

key_findings.finding: Theoretically, the reverse-process sample's SNR is provably below the forward SNR at every timestep, formalizing the SNR-t bias.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 5.1 derives SNR(t) = γ̂_t^2 ᾱ_t / (1 - ᾱ_t + (√ᾱ_t β_{t+1} φ_{t+1}/(1-ᾱ_{t+1}))^2) with 0 < γ̂_t ≤ 1, versus forward ᾱ_t/(1-ᾱ_t); equivalently x̂_{t-1} = γ̂_{t-1} x_{t-1} + ψ_{t-1} ε.

key_findings.finding: The prior assumption x_θ^0 = x_0 + φ_t ε is inconsistent; the reconstruction must be scaled (γ_t ≤ 1) reflecting information loss.
key_findings.evidence: Via Tweedie's formula the reconstruction equals the posterior mean, so E||x_θ^0||^2 ≤ E||x_0||^2, contradicting E||x_θ^0||^2 = E||x_0||^2 + φ_t^2; measured norms of x_θ^0 in both forward and reverse processes fall below ||x_0||^2.

key_findings.finding: DCW improves generation quality across diverse DPMs, samplers and resolutions at essentially zero cost, especially in few-step regimes.
key_findings.evidence: FID drops e.g. IDDPM CIFAR-10 13.19 to 7.57 at 20 steps (-42.6%) and 5.55 to 4.16 at 50 steps; EDM 10.66 to 5.67 at 13 NFE (-47%); DiT ImageNet 256 12.83 to 7.99 at 20 steps; Recall also improves; added runtime is 0.08-0.47% with no extra NFE.

key_findings.finding: DCW is complementary to and stronger than existing exposure-bias correctors.
key_findings.evidence: It beats DPM-AE and DPM-AT on all DDIM/ADM CIFAR-10 settings (e.g. ADM 10 steps: 13.01 vs 15.88 for AT); stacked on ADM-ES and DPM-FR it still cuts FID further (EDM-ES by 7.0/5.3/3.5% at 13/21/35 NFE; PFGM-FR by 6.6/5.7/2.0%).
